THE LONG HONEY BRASS: an enormously long brass telescope in a forked timber cradle, its worn honey body reaching as far across the room as the rolling ladder is tall, angled so one end recedes deep into the frame, a coil of rope hung over the cradle's near horn.

THE GREAT LONG ONE IN AMBER LIGHT: an enormously long brass telescope swinging in a forked timber cradle, its long brass body as long as the room is wide, turned at an angle so the far end vanishes into shadow, brass worn bright where hands grip it nearest the narrow lower end.

THE LONG ONE WITH THE BELL: an enormously long brass telescope in a forked timber cradle, its honey brass body reaching as far as the rolling ladder's top rung, canted off-centre, a little brass bell on a short cord tied to the cradle's horn, rung whenever the whole thing swings round.

THE LONG BRASS WITH THE WEDGE: an enormously long brass telescope in a forked timber cradle, its body as long as the room is wide, angled steeply so the narrow lower end hangs near the boards, a wooden wedge kicked under the cradle's foot to stop it drifting in flat dithered shadow.

THE LONG ONE WRAPPED AGAINST THE COLD: an enormously long brass telescope in a forked timber cradle, its body reaching as far as the rolling ladder is tall, turned so one end steps back into the picture, the crank's handle wrapped tight in a strip of dark cloth, worn pale at the centre of the grip.

THE FAT DRUM IN THE IRON RING: a short thick brass telescope slung in a heavy iron ring that turns, as broad through as three floorboards, its wide open end filling one side of the picture, a brass end cap hanging off it on a short chain, swinging slightly.

THE FAT DRUM WITH THE CORD: a short thick brass telescope slung in a heavy iron ring that turns, as thick through as two floorboards are wide, its great wide end angled toward the slot, a second small telescope strapped alongside the big one with three cords, one of them knotted twice.

THE FAT DRUM IN DEEP GOLD: a short thick brass telescope slung in a heavy iron ring, as broad as four floorboards, its brass body in flat stepped bands of deep honey and shadow, a step worn hollow in the iron ring's lower bracket where boots have pushed up against it for fifty years.

THE FAT DRUM ON THE IRON RING WITH THE ROPE: a short thick brass telescope slung in a heavy iron ring that turns, its body as thick through as three floorboards, canted off-centre so the wide open end looms at one side, a rope's end bound in bright red thread dangling from the ring's lower horn.

THE STONE PIER SCOPE: a great brass telescope rising off a squat stone pier, its long brass body reaching two thirds of the way up the dome, the boards fitted close round the pier's foot, turned at an angle with the narrow lower end stepping back into the frame, a worn hollow scooped in the pier's top stone by fifty years of the brass heel shifting.

THE PIER SCOPE WITH THE COUNTERWEIGHT ARM: a great brass telescope rising off a squat stone pier, its body as tall as the curved wall is high, the whole thing turned so one side recedes, a heavy iron counterweight hanging off a short arm at the heel, its flat face catching a hard pixel band of lamplight.

THE PIER SCOPE IN BLOCKY STONE: a great brass telescope rising off a squat stone pier of blocky stacked stone courses, reaching two thirds of the way up the dome, angled off-centre, the boards notched tight round the pier's base, a worn groove cut into the pier's top edge where the brass heel has rocked back and forth.

THE STONE PIER WITH THE SECOND SCOPE: a great brass telescope rising off a squat stone pier, its body as long as the room is wide, turned so the narrow lower end steps back into the frame, a second small telescope strapped alongside the big one with cord, its own narrow end aimed a fraction higher than the big one's.

THE COUNTERWEIGHTED BEAM IN AMBER: a great brass telescope balanced across a heavy timber beam, its long brass body as long as the beam itself, canted off-centre with the wide open end riding high, a great iron counterweight hanging off the heel on a short arm, its flat iron face in three flat stepped bands of shadow.

THE COUNTERWEIGHTED BEAM WITH THE BRIGHT CRANK: a great brass telescope balanced across a heavy timber beam, reaching as far as the beam is long, angled so one end recedes into the frame, a great iron counterweight at the heel, the crank handle painted a vivid vermilion, its colour rubbed pale at the very tip where fingers always take hold.

THE COUNTERWEIGHTED BEAM AND THE WORN BOARD: a great brass telescope balanced across a heavy timber beam, its brass body as long as the beam, swung off-centre with the wide end high, a heavy iron counterweight hanging at the heel, and in the boards directly below the wheel a worn hollow ground dark and deep by years of turning.

THE COUNTERWEIGHTED BEAM ON THE LEAN: a great brass telescope balanced across a heavy timber beam, as long as the beam itself, canted sharply off-centre so the wide open end towers over the rolling ladder's top rung, a great iron counterweight at the heel, a rope's end coiled over the beam's far horn and bound in bright yellow thread.

THE CRANK-AND-WHEEL IN FLAT PIXEL BANDS: a great brass telescope beside a toothed iron wheel reaching two thirds of the way up the dome, the whole machine turned at an angle with one side receding, the hand crank jutting toward the viewer, its iron teeth casting hard pixel steps of shadow, the brass body worn to a bright streak where the same hand grips it every clear night.

THE CRANK-AND-WHEEL WITH THE BELL: a great brass telescope and a toothed iron wheel as long as the room is wide, swung together off-centre, the crank's handle wrapped in cloth, a small brass bell fixed to the wheel's upper spoke so it rings against an iron pin with every full turn, its clapper worn bright at the tip.

THE CRANK-AND-WHEEL AND THE WORN GROOVE: a great brass telescope turning with a toothed iron wheel reaching most of the way up the dome, the machine canted off-centre so the wide open end rises over the frame, the hand crank jutting out, a deep groove worn into the boards in a wide arc where the wheel's foot has ground round and round for years.

THE CRANK-AND-WHEEL WITH THE VIVID HANDLE: a great brass telescope swinging with a toothed iron wheel that stands as tall as the rolling ladder, the whole rig angled so one side steps back into shadow in flat dithered bands, the crank's handle painted a deep cobalt blue, the paint cracked and bright at the knuckle of the grip.

THE DOME-HUNG SCOPE IN IRON CHAIN: a great brass telescope slung on iron chains and pulleys from the dome's own ribs, hanging above the boards, its long brass body angled so the wide open end aims up through the slot, one chain longer than the other so the whole thing tilts, a brass end cap on a short chain swinging below the narrow lower end.

THE DOME-HUNG SCOPE WITH THE BRIGHT PULLEY: a great brass telescope slung on ropes and iron pulleys from the dome's own ribs, its brass body hanging free above the boards, as long as the room is wide, canted off-centre, one pulley wheel larger than the other two, worn so bright at its crown it throws a hard flat pixel highlight.

THE DOME-HUNG SCOPE WITH THE KNOTTED ROPE: a great brass telescope hanging on chains and iron pulleys from the dome's ribs above the boards, its long brass body angled so the narrow lower end rides near the ladder's top rung, a rope's end hanging below one pulley and knotted three times, the lowest knot wound tight in a strip of bright green cord.

THE DOME-HUNG SCOPE WITH THE SECOND GLASS: a great brass telescope slung on iron chains from the dome's own ribs, hanging above the boards so the wide open end aims at the slot, reaching two thirds of the way up the dome, turned at an angle with one side stepping into shadow, a second small telescope strapped alongside the big one with cord, aimed a fraction to the side.
